# LucidDOM.js

LucidDOM.js is a lightweight browser-side DOM helper. It wraps a parent element and provides methods for creating elements, selecting descendants, updating content, handling events, applying inline styles, and removing elements.

## Installation

### npm

Install LucidDOM from npm:

```sh
npm install luciddom
```

Import the default export in your app. Use a bundler that resolves npm packages:

```html
<div id="app"></div>
<script type="module" src="./app.js"></script>
```

```js
// app.js
import LucidDOM from 'luciddom';

const app = new LucidDOM(document.querySelector('#app'));

const message = app.addElement({
    tag: 'p',
    className: 'message',
    value: 'Hello from LucidDOM!'
});

message.styles({ color: 'darkslateblue', fontWeight: 'bold' });
```

### unpkg CDN

For a browser module without an npm install or bundler, import the package directly from unpkg:

```html
<div id="app"></div>
<script type="module">
    import LucidDOM from 'https://unpkg.com/luciddom@1.0.1/lucidDOM.js';

    const app = new LucidDOM(document.querySelector('#app'));
    app.addElement({
        tag: 'p',
        value: 'Hello from LucidDOM!'
    });
</script>
```

The constructor accepts a DOM element and scopes queries and element creation to it. If no parent is passed, it defaults to `document.body`.

## Common operations

### Select and update

```js
const heading = app.select('h1');

if (heading.current) {
    heading.update({ value: 'Welcome', className: 'page-title' });
    heading.styles({ color: 'darkslateblue' });
}
```

`select(selector)` uses `querySelector()` within the configured parent. The returned handle's `current` property is `null` when no element matches, so check it before using the handle.

### Listen for events

```js
const button = app.select('#submit');

function submitForm() {
    console.log('Submitted');
}

button.on('click', submitForm);
// Later, remove the same listener with the same function reference:
button.off('click', submitForm);
```

`on()` and `off()` are also available on the `LucidDOM` instance and act on its parent element.

### Create and remove elements

```js
const item = app.addElement({
    tag: 'li',
    className: 'todo-item',
    value: 'Read the documentation'
});

item.on('click', () => console.log('Item clicked'));
item.remove();
```

## API overview

| API | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `new LucidDOM(parent?)` | Create an instance scoped to `parent`, defaulting to `document.body`. |
| `app.addElement(options)` | Create and append an element; returns a handle for events, styles, and removal. |
| `app.select(selector)` | Select the first matching descendant and return a handle with `current`. |
| `app.selectAll(selector)` | Select all matching descendants; `current` is the native `NodeList` and handle methods apply to every match. |
| `app.on(event, callback)` / `app.off(event, callback)` | Add or remove a listener on the parent element. |
| `app.styles(styleObject)` | Apply inline CSS styles to the parent element. |
| `handle.update(options)` | Update content and supported attributes on a selected element. |
| `handle.addClass(name)` / `handle.removeClass(name)` | Add or remove a class on a selected element. |
| `handle.remove()` | Remove the handled element from the DOM. |

`addElement()` accepts a required `tag` and these optional properties: `className`, `id`, `value`, `type`, `placeholder`, `name`, `htmlFor`, `formAction`, `formMethod`, `formTarget`, `formEnctype`, `formNoValidate`, `ariaLabel`, `title`, and `html`.

`value` sets text content (and the element's value property). `html` sets `innerHTML`; only pass trusted or sanitized markup. Prefer `value` for plain text.

## Working with multiple matches

The handle from `selectAll()` applies its helper methods to each matching element. It supports event listeners, inline styles, adding and removing classes, updating supported attributes and content, removing the matches, and adding a child to each match.

```js
const items = app.selectAll('.todo-item');

items.styles({ color: 'darkslateblue' });
items.addClass('is-visible');
items.update({ title: 'Visible item' });
items.on('click', (event) => {
    console.log('Clicked:', event.currentTarget);
});

// `current` remains a native NodeList for custom per-element work.
items.current.forEach((item) => {
    console.log(item.textContent);
});
```

When nothing matches, `current` is an empty NodeList and helper methods do nothing. `select()` returns a handle even when there is no match; check `handle.current` before calling methods on that handle.

## Build

The package includes an esbuild script to create a minified browser bundle:

```sh
npm install
npm run build
```

The output is written to `dist/luciddom.min.js`.
